label: models/fw_valvewheel.mdl: a valve wheel, red paint worn to steel at the rim

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/big_rock.mdl, models/miniturret.mdl, models/uplant2.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked A, B, D, B where the asset was C, A, B, D: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: The wheel's outline matches the brief's words: a round valve wheel, face-on in FRONT and BACK, about 12 facets round the rim, with the spokes and hub in the middle. A stand, base and arm sit under and behind it (LEFT, RIGHT, BELOW). The brief does not ask for them and they do not change the wheel's outline, so they are not charged here.

M2.reason: Across is 32.1 units against the brief's 32, which is within 0.5 percent and well inside the 15% band. Depth is 17 and height 40.1; the height includes the pillar and base the brief does not ask for, so only the across is held to the brief.

M3.reason: The parts the brief names are all present: the rim (a steel ring, about 12 facets, in the front and back views), the red spokes (six, reaching the rim in the front view), and the red hub at the centre, with the hub boss standing off the wheel face in the left and right views. The brief names no spoke count or rim facet count, so none can be charged. The pillar and base are not in the brief and are charged under M1, not here.

M4.reason: The rim is a pale worn steel grey and the spokes and hub are red, as the brief asks. The pillar and base are green-grey with dark rust patches, which fits the station's rusted steel. The colours are plain and match the brief.

M5.reason: The wear the brief asks for is there: red paint is worn off the rim, and the spokes show some scuffing in FRONT and FRONT-LEFT. The stand has grime and weathering. The wear is light, but it is in the places the brief names.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the rubric: M6 is measured apart in the line-up test, not judged here.

M7.reason: The wheel faces the front, the spokes are upright, and the base sits flat on the bottom, so the model stands on its origin. The brief gives no facing, so this is judged on the model alone.

M8.reason: SMAK's check passes with no errors. The model has 324 triangles, above twice the median of Half-Life's props of its kind (99 median, so 198), but below the 422 that is the most Valve spends on its kind, and under the amended rule that is the line a model fails past. The rim, spokes, hub, pillar and base read closed from every view, and the bottom of the base is a closed plate in the below view.
